# **Comparative Analysis of Frontier Neural Audio Architectures for Local Apple Silicon Deployment and Real-Time Demonstration**

## **Candidate Paper Evaluation and Benchmarking**

The selection of a neural audio architecture for a graduate-level review, reproduction, and empirical evaluation project requires balancing architectural novelty, computational efficiency, and ease of live demonstration. On an Apple Silicon M4 Pro architecture equipped with 24 GB of unified memory, models must execute inference using PyTorch via Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) or CPU fallbacks, without relying on proprietary CUDA extensions or memory-intensive backbones.  
The table below details candidate papers published between 2024 and 2026 across top venues including ICLR, ICASSP, ACL, and IEEE/ACM TASLP. Each candidate is benchmarked on model footprint, inference latency, baseline comparability, metric evaluation, and local execution feasibility.

## **Theoretical Synthesis and Architectural Paradigms**

The evaluated candidates reflect a technical shift in neural audio processing toward flow matching, single-codebook vector quantization, structural frequency decomposition, and joint magnitude-phase spectral modeling.  
In discrete audio tokenization, historical architectures such as EnCodec and SoundStream rely on multi-codebook Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ), allocating audio bandwidth across 8 to 16 quantizers and generating sequence lengths of 300 to 600 tokens per second1. WavTokenizer re-evaluates this paradigm by proving that a single-codebook quantization space, when paired with an expanded decoder network and multi-scale discriminators, can absorb rich acoustic and semantic representations at bitrates down to 40 tokens per second1. This structural reduction in token density reduces sequence lengths for downstream speech-language modeling without sacrificing reconstruction fidelity1.  
In generative speech synthesis, non-autoregressive Flow Matching architectures like F5-TTS and Matcha-TTS eliminate traditional autoregressive generation loops and score-based diffusion trajectories9. Autoregressive models suffer from sequential sampling latency and error propagation, whereas standard score-based diffusion requires dozens of reverse-time sampling steps35. Flow matching formulates a straight-line vector field between a standard Gaussian distribution and the target data distribution, enabling Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) solvers to sample high-fidelity audio in minimal numerical integration steps9. F5-TTS simplifies this pipeline by removing complex text aligners, phonemizers, and duration predictors, relying on sequence infilling within a ConvNeXt V2 Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone9.  
For music source separation, Band-Split RoFormer (BS-RoFormer) advances beyond conventional UNet spectrogram masking14. Standard neural separators process short-time Fourier transform (STFT) grids uniformly using 2D convolutions, ignoring the non-linear harmonic structure of musical intervals14. BS-RoFormer divides the complex spectrogram into distinct, non-overlapping frequency bands and maps them to subband representations15. Stacked Transformer layers model inner-band temporal variations and inter-band spectral relationships, while Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) maintain long-range temporal coherence across variable-length musical tracks14.  
In single-channel speech enhancement, MP-SENet resolves phase estimation inconsistencies27. Traditional deep learning denoisers predict real-valued magnitude masks and reuse the corrupted phase from the noisy input waveform, which creates phase mismatch artifacts27. MP-SENet establishes a dual-path architecture where magnitude spectral masks are estimated via dilated DenseNets while continuous phase spectra are synthesized via a joint Time-Frequency Transformer27. This parallel estimation prevents phase compensation errors, yielding clean speech under non-stationary noise conditions27.

## **Top Three Ranked Recommendations**

### **Rank 1: WavTokenizer (ICLR 2025\)**

WavTokenizer represents the strongest match for a 4-week graduate project executed on an Apple Silicon M4 Pro1. The official repository provides pre-trained weights (ranging from 120 MB to 400 MB) and clean inference scripts (inference.py) that run natively on MPS and CPU without custom CUDA kernel dependencies1.  
Inference processing on a 5-second 24 kHz audio file completes in under 0.3 seconds while consuming less than 2 GB of unified memory1. The live demonstration provides a immediate "wow" factor by compressing continuous audio into 40 discrete tokens per second and decoding it back into high-fidelity audio1. This output can be directly benchmarked against classical STFT overlap-add reconstruction and standard G.722 codecs3.  
The primary operational risk is the strict input audio sample rate constraint (exact 24 kHz mono), which requires building a reliable pre-processing resampling wrapper using torchaudio1.

### **Rank 2: F5-TTS (ACL 2025\)**

F5-TTS offers an exceptional balance of structural novelty and real-time demonstration capability for zero-shot text-to-speech synthesis and voice cloning8. Its non-autoregressive Flow Matching framework replaces multi-stage pipelines by projecting text and reference audio into continuous vector fields using a ConvNeXt V2 Diffusion Transformer9.  
The model fits comfortably within the 24 GB unified memory allocation (\~4 GB peak VRAM during inference) and executes a 5-second synthesis request in under 2.5 seconds on Mac MPS7. A live audience member can record a short 5-second voice prompt, type a text phrase, and generate cloned speech during a talk9. The generated sample can be compared directly against a classical Griffin-Lim spectrogram inversion baseline9.  
The main technical risk involves tuning the Euler ODE solver steps: setting evaluations too low (\<16 steps) creates audible phase artifacts, while setting them too high (\>50 steps) extends latency beyond the real-time presentation budget35.

### **Rank 3: Band-Split RoFormer (ICASSP 2024\)**

Band-Split RoFormer stands as the state-of-the-art benchmark for high-fidelity music source separation13. Using the standalone bs-roformer-infer package, execution requires no complex GUI dependencies and runs seamlessly on Mac MPS with a lightweight \~350 MB checkpoint13.  
The model processes complex stereo audio tracks in 2 to 3 seconds, isolating vocals, drums, bass, and accompaniment with clean spectral separation14. During a live demonstration, separating a commercial song into clean isolated stems provides an impactful auditory comparison against a classical Short-Time Fourier Transform Wiener filter baseline14.  
The primary project risk stems from memory scaling over long audio inputs due to subband self-attention overhead15. Implementing an automated audio chunking script (10-to-15-second sub-windows with overlap-add windowing) is required to prevent memory paging on 24 GB hardware.

## **Empirical Roadmap and Baseline Evaluation Protocols**

To complete the project within a 4-week window, development should progress systematically across environment setup, baseline implementation, neural inference integration, and formal quantitative evaluation.

### **Implementation of Classical Baselines**

To establish comparative benchmarks against the neural models, specific mathematical baselines must be implemented from first principles:

#### **Speech Denoising Baseline (Wiener Filtering)**

Given a noisy spectral frame ![][image1], the Minimum Mean-Square Error (MMSE) Wiener filter estimates the clean speech magnitude spectrum ![][image2] by estimating the noise power spectral density ![][image3] from initial non-speech frames:  
![][image4]  
![][image5]

#### **Source Separation Baseline (STFT Spectral Masking)**

Calculates soft energy ratio masks across stereo channels or frequency subbands to isolate target source components:  
![][image6]  
![][image7]

#### **Speech Synthesis Baseline (Griffin-Lim Algorithm)**

Reconstructs temporal phase iteratively from a target mel-spectrogram magnitude ![][image8] via alternating Short-Time Fourier Transform (![][image9]) and inverse STFT (![][image10]) operations:  
![][image11]

### **Empirical Evaluation Workflow**

> 1. **Standardized Dataset Evaluation**: Evaluate performance across a 100-sample slice of official dataset test splits (such as LibriTTS for codecs/TTS, MUSDB18-HQ for source separation, or VoiceBank+DEMAND for enhancement)1.  
> 2. **Custom Audio Evaluation**: Collect 10 custom microphone recordings captured under real-world conditions (e.g., quiet room, office environment, background cafeteria noise).  
> 3. **Metric Execution**: Run automated metric scripts (pesq for PESQ scores, pystoi for STOI, museval for SI-SDR, and openai-whisper for Word Error Rate) across both the classical baseline outputs and the neural model outputs12. Log execution latency per second of processed audio to verify real-time performance on Apple Silicon MPS hardware.
